faqs.q: What kind of game is Directive 8020?
faqs.a: It is a cinematic science-fiction horror adventure from Supermassive Games. The crew of the Cassiopeia faces an alien capable of mimicking people, and your decisions shape the story.
Lashana Lynch portrays Brianna Young, a pilot aboard the Cassiopeia.
The official description of Turning Points confirms that players can return to key decisions to explore different outcomes. This does not establish a guaranteed route to any particular ending.

Yes. A free update on 19 October 2026 added online multiplayer to the PS5, Xbox Series X|S and Steam versions. Up to five players can connect from separate locations, and each player must own a copy; no friend pass or crossplay has been announced. See the [multiplayer guide](/multiplayer).

faqs.q: How do you save Williams in Directive 8020?
faqs.a: Sedate him in Episode 5's “Suspicions” section: agree with Anders and prepare the diazepam sedative (code 168). Then choose Stand Down at the Point Blank standoff in Episode 6. That unlocks **Is This Decaf?** and **Suspect Acquitted**. Full route: [Shoot Williams or Stand Down?](/shoot-williams-or-stand-down).

faqs.q: How do you get the best ending in Directive 8020?
faqs.a: There is no official “best ending” label. The outcome that ending guides call best is the Homeward Bound escape: the crew reaches the vacant Cassiopeia and sets course for Earth. It requires saving the crew in Episode 6, keeping Young's **Loyal** trait above **Serious** at the start of Episode 8, choosing humanity over survival at the birthday-cake wish, and escaping in the shuttle with at least one survivor. See [all endings](/all-endings).

faqs.q: How do you get to the abandoned ship instead of the Ring?
faqs.a: The abandoned ship is the vacant Cassiopeia, reached through the same Homeward Bound route: save the crew in Episode 6, keep Young's **Loyal** trait above **Serious** at the start of Episode 8, and choose humanity over survival at the birthday-cake wish. If you choose survival first, the survivors head to the Booster Ring instead. [GIGA's ending guide](https://www.giga.de/games/directive-8020-alle-enden-erklaert-so-schaltet-ihr-das-beste-und-schlimmste-finale-frei--01KRXRD6TFCKM16CWKFGQVMM2D) documents the step-by-step route.

faqs.q: What game is coming after Directive 8020?
faqs.a: No next game has been officially confirmed. Collecting all “O Death” objects unlocks a teaser in the Bonus Content menu; the community widely speculates it is **The Craven Man**, but Supermassive has not confirmed the title or a release date. See [GameRant's teaser breakdown](https://gamerant.com/dark-pictures-anthology-next-game-teaser/).

faqs.q: What was the budget of Directive 8020?
faqs.a: Supermassive and Bandai Namco have not published a budget or development cost for Directive 8020. Any specific number you see online is an estimate, not an official figure.

It is not universally considered bad, but reviews were mixed: at launch, Metacritic averaged 71 and OpenCritic 76, with 62% of critics recommending it. Common criticisms are the repetitive stealth sections, a story described as not particularly gripping, and uneven characters; reviewers praised the atmosphere, cast and Turning Points. See [TheGamer's review roundup](https://www.thegamer.com/directive-8020-dark-pictures-anthology-mixed-reviews/).

faqs.q: What ending did Jenn get in Directive 8020?
faqs.a: Jenn is not a character in Directive 8020. The five playable crew members are Young, Stafford, Eisele, Cernan and Cooper; if you mean a creator's playthrough, the ending depends on the choices they made. See the [character guide](/characters).
